proposal: The Mandate recommends that the next administration refocus the Federal Highway Administration on maintaining and improving the highway system, remove or reform rules that hamper state governments, and reduce federal involvement in local decisions. It criticizes the prior administration's emphasis on equity, carbon dioxide obligations on states, and a guidance memo discouraging highway capacity expansion.

status_summary: FHWA published a final rule on 2025-04-18 (90 FR 16463), effective 2025-05-19, repealing the greenhouse gas measure that required states and metropolitan planning organizations to set declining carbon dioxide targets. A memorandum of 2025-03-07 from the FHWA Chief Counsel rescinded in full the 2021-12-16 memo urging use of infrastructure law funds on existing infrastructure and its 2023-02-24 update, and said FHWA was reviewing all of its infrastructure law guidance. USDOT announced 16 FHWA deregulatory actions on 2025-05-29, and FHWA later published final rules removing several regulations, including 23 CFR parts 970 and 971 (2025-11-17) and 23 CFR part 633 subpart A (91 FR 25492, 2026-05-11), which are administrative clean-ups rather than relief from named state obligations. An undated Eno Transportation Weekly article also reports that strategic priority sections were removed from program guidance reissued from April 2026; the broader refocusing and reduction of federal involvement in local projects is not shown in the sources found.

timeline.event: The FHWA Chief Counsel issues a memorandum rescinding in full the 2021-12-16 Build a Better America policy memo on use of infrastructure law resources and its 2023-02-24 update, and states that FHWA is reviewing all of its infrastructure law guidance.
FHWA publishes a final rule (90 FR 16463, RIN 2125-AG16) repealing the greenhouse gas measure in 23 CFR part 490, including the declining carbon dioxide target and reporting requirement.
The greenhouse gas measure repeal took effect.

The U.S. Department of Transportation announced 52 deregulatory actions, most of them at the proposed-rule stage, 16 of them by FHWA (15 rescissions and 1 withdrawal), including proposed removal of the 23 CFR part 500 management systems rule and of the form-inclusion requirement in 23 CFR part 633, and a final rule on the state highway agency equal employment opportunity plan-submission requirement in 23 CFR part 230 subpart C.

FHWA published a final rule (90 FR 22852, document 2025-09725) rescinding the first-performance-period provisions of 23 CFR part 490 subpart A, issued without notice and comment and effective the same day.

FHWA published final rules removing 23 CFR part 660 subpart A and rescinding the management systems rules in 23 CFR parts 970 and 971 (documents 2025-19905, 2025-19906 and the part 971 rule; the parts 970 and 971 rules effective 2025-12-17), stating the systems can be implemented without regulations.

FHWA published a final rule (91 FR 25492, document 2026-09276, effective 2026-06-10) rescinding 23 CFR part 633 subpart A, which ended the requirement to physically include Form FHWA-1273 in each Federal-aid construction contract.

title: Refocus FHWA on highways; drop the carbon target rule and capacity guidance memo
uncertainties: The recommendation is broad, so the record tracks the specific items named (the carbon target rule and the guidance memo). The rescission memorandum was read on transportation.gov and is dated 2025-03-07; a news report dated 2025-03-11 describes the action as taken the Monday before, likely the date it was announced. A correction to the final rule (Doc. 2025-08352, 2025-05-13) was not read. The report of later guidance revisions rests on an undated Eno Transportation Weekly article. No count of other FHWA rules removed was made, and the equity item was not tracked separately. Update of 2026-11-10: the USDOT release of 2025-05-29 was read on highways.dot.gov; the final rules of 2025-05-30 and 2025-11-17 were read on govinfo.gov (the November rules in part, as an excerpt); and 91 FR 25492 and the FHWA memorandum of 2026-06-29 were read on federalregister.gov and fhwa.dot.gov. The federalregister.gov page for document 2025-19906 could not be opened on federalregister.gov in this review. These rescissions mostly remove obsolete or duplicative rules and the release describes most of the other FHWA items as proposed removals whose later finalization was not traced; they are treated as partial support for the item on rules that hamper states, and stage and progress are unchanged.
